english.title: Intentionally alter / destroy / conceal etc information to prevent disclosure to data subject
english.standardoffencewording:

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution only by the Commissioner or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii)This offence applies where a request has been made in the exercise of a data subject access right, and the person making the request would have been entitled to receive information in response to that request.
(iii) See section 173(2) for the meaning of 'data subject access right'.
(iv) Section 173(5) gives the defences for a person charged with this offence, which are that the alteration, defacing, blocking, erasure, destruction or concealment would have occurred in the absence of a request made in exercise of a data subject access right, or, that the person acted in the reasonable belief that the person making the request was not entitled to receive the information in response to the request.
(v) Where this offence has been committed by a body corporate, and it is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of or to be attributable to neglect on the part of a director, manager, secretary or similar officer of the body corporate, or a person who was purporting to act in such a capacity, the director, manager, secretary, as well as the body corporate is guilty of the offence and proceedings can also be taken against them.
(vi) Section 199(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 states that the National Police Records (Recordable Offences) Regulations 2000 (S.I. 2000/1139) has effect as if this offence was listed in the Schedule to the Regulations. Therefore offenders must be fingerprinted and photographed as well as the offence being PNC recordable.
